messages:
alex_r: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-select rollout we're seeing unexpected KV cache behavior on INT8 profiles. p95 memory for transformer-prod spiked and KV hit-rate dropped. Repro below.
perf-bot: alert: kv_hit_rate_drop model=rw-large variant=int8 p95_mem_incr=1.1GB kv_hit_pct_before=88.9 kv_hit_pct_after=57.2
maria_s: can you paste the smallest repro? which kernel change landed?
alex_r: landed: runtime/kernel-selector#812 (prefer 'agg-cluster' kernels for short sequences). Repro script (dev rig):
```
# repro load
ab -n 1000 -c 8 -H "x-model: rw-large/int8" http://localhost:8080/v1/generate
```
also attaching short log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T21:03:12Z] kv: slot_allocs=42k slots_used=31k slabs=64k pages_evicted=7.2k prefetched=1.1k
[2026-03-17T21:03:12Z] mem: p95=3.7GB -> 4.85GB
```
alex_r: quick metrics: before rollout kv_hit=89%, avg_tokens/sec=240; after kv_hit=56%, avg_tokens/sec=190; eval-regression on our promptset: mean-accuracy -0.7% (not huge but consistent)
jen_k: looks bad. any sign of increased fragmentation or more frequent slab reclamation?
sanjay_p: initial hunch: agg-cluster kernel changes page access pattern for compressed INT8 slot packing. Prefetch heuristic assumes uniform slot density. If packed density varies with quantization, prefetch window can over/under-shoot -> more page churn and lower reuse.
alex_r: i dumped slot occupancy histograms from the runtime (snippet):
```
slot_density_buckets: {0-25%: 12%, 25-50%: 18%, 50-75%: 44%, 75-100%: 26%}
post-rollout (int8): {0-25%: 34%, 25-50%: 30%, 50-75%: 26%, 75-100%: 10%}
```
maria_s: that shift toward low-density slots would explain more pages per kv entry and smaller useful prefetch strides.
sanjay_p: two quick experiments:
- toggle prefetch_window from 128 -> 48 for int8 and measure p95 mem and kv_hit
- force kernel-selector to fallback to old policy for int8 and compare
alex_r: ran both locally. results in ~10 minutes each:
- prefetch=48: kv_hit -> 78%, p95 mem down 600MB, throughput back to 225 t/s
- kernel fallback: kv_hit -> 86%, p95 mem almost fully restored
jen_k: can we do a canary rollback for int8 models only while we fix heuristics?
deploy-bot: canary rollouts supported per-model/variant. starting canary: variant=rw-large/int8 scope=10% target=us-west-2
perf-bot: canary metrics (10m): kv_hit now 84.7% on canary, p95 mem within 4% of pre-rollout baseline, errors unchanged
alex_r: good. short-term mitigation: pin kernel-selector to previous policy for quantized variants (int8,bf16) until we update prefetcher to consult slot_density telemetry.
sanjay_p: long-term fix ideas:
- expose slot_density histogram in hot telemetry and use density-aware prefetch window computation (window = base * (avg_slot_bytes / slot_page_bytes))
- add a cheap online estimator of slot packing to kernel selector so it can pick kernels that preserve locality for high-fragmentation cases
- consider compact-coalescer background pass when fragmentation crosses threshold
maria_s: also recommend adding an A/B test across several model sizes; packing behavior likely varies by model and tokenizer.
jen_k: will open tracking RFC and patch. can we add a flag `runtime.int8.prefetch_mode=conservative` for quick toggles?
alex_r: yep I'll push a small flag PR and a telemetry dashboard with slot histograms + kv_hit by quantization.
perf-bot: note: add metric `kv_prefetch_mispredict_rate` and `slot_density_p95` to the alert rules.
deploy-bot: canary finished: status=success rolled back for affected variants to kernel=pre-agg-20260316
alex_r: tl;dr: kernel selection change exposed a sensitivity in the prefetch/batching heuristics for quantized page layouts -> increased fragmentation/paging -> mem growth and hit-rate drop. mitigation = per-variant kernel pin + conservative prefetch mode. Next: implement density-aware prefetcher and run cross-model sweep. Ticket: INF-4821 (I'll link PRs in there). :+1:
maria_s: thanks. great catch, team. small note: include eval promptset baseline in ticket so we can guard against subtle accuracy deltas when changing heuristics.
